Alastair Campbell:
Alastair Campbell holds the lowest winning score in Legs Open history. His four-under-par nett at Carnwath in 2013 has not been matched in the thirteen championships since, and only Kevin Park, three under at St Andrews in 2020, has finished within a shot of it.

That opening championship was very nearly a clean sweep. Campbell's 75 was the low gross of the day, taking the Scratch title alongside the Main, and his 40 Stableford points were the best in the field — a tally only Bobby Ferguson has equalled, in the same year. The rule barring the Main champion from also taking the Stableford was all that stopped him holding all three.

He returned to finish tied second at Lanark in 2015 and tied sixth at Blairgowrie in 2021, and played five championships in all between 2013 and 2021.
David Clee:
David Clee is one of only two men to have won the Legs Open twice, and he did it back to back — a defence matched since only by Andrew Duncan. The pair of titles could hardly be less alike.

The first, at Lanark in 2015, came at four over par. The second, at Southerness in 2016, came at seventeen over — the highest winning score the championship has recorded, by some distance, and a number that tells its own story about the day. He took the Scratch title that year as well, with a gross of 101.

Twelve appearances between 2013 and 2026 make him one of the most familiar figures in the field, and he has been competitive across all of them: tied third on debut in 2013, fourth at Gullane in 2018, fifth at Ladybank in 2019 and fifth again at Balmedie in 2025. His handicap has come down from 17 to 6 across those years.
Andrew Duncan:
Andrew Duncan is one of two men to have successfully defended the Legs Open, after David Clee a decade earlier. Level par at Downfield in 2024, level par again at Balmedie in 2025 — back-to-back titles, and the second of them completed with the low gross of 75 to take the Scratch as well.

He had been building towards it. Second at Ladybank in 2019 on his debut, where he also won the Stableford with 35 points, then fourth at St Andrews in 2020 and tied second at Loch Lomond in 2022.

The seven appearances have coincided with a severe reduction in handicap, from 12 to 1, which makes the two level-par nett rounds a considerably harder piece of work at the end than they would have been at the start.
Colin Howieson:
Colin Howieson won the Legs Open at Dalmahoy in 2017 at two over par, and took the Scratch title the same day with a gross of 79.

He came close to a second at Panmure in 2023, finishing tied for the title on one over before losing the countback — but took the Stableford that year with 35 points, and posted a 78 that remains his lowest gross round.

His eight appearances have been interrupted ones: he has failed to return a card in four of them, including three of the last five. When he has finished, he has rarely been far away.
Bryan Forbes:
Bryan Forbes won the Legs Open at Ladybank in 2019 at one under par, one of only four championships in fourteen to have been won under par.

It was a thorough afternoon's work. He also took the Scratch with a 79 — still his lowest round — and led the Stableford on 38 points, a total bettered only four times in the championship's history.

Eight consecutive appearances from 2019 to 2026 make him one of the most reliable men in the field, with a fifth at St Andrews in 2020 and tied ninths at Loch Lomond in 2022 and Castle Stuart in 2026.
Kevin Park:
Kevin Park's win at St Andrews in 2020 came at three under par, the second-lowest winning score the Legs Open has seen.

He led the Stableford that day too, with 39 points — a figure only Alastair Campbell and Bobby Ferguson have beaten, both in 2013. Fourth at Ladybank the year before and tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025 are the closest he has come to repeating it.

Across eight appearances his handicap has fallen from 26 to 15, and at 64 he is among the oldest men to have lifted the trophy.
Nick Ward:
Nick Ward won the Legs Open at Blairgowrie in 2021, at two under par, on his first appearance.

He took the Scratch title in the same round with a gross of 80, and his 38 Stableford points would have won that competition too had the Main champion not been barred from it. Only two men have won the championship with a lower score.

He has played twice more since, finishing 12th at Loch Lomond in 2022 and 16th at Downfield in 2024.
Lloyd Swan:
Lloyd Swan won the Legs Open at Loch Lomond in 2022 on his debut, returning a level-par nett 72 to finish two clear of a four-way tie behind him.

His 36 Stableford points were the best in the field, and his gross of 82 was fifth. He returned the following year at Panmure to finish fifth, and has not played since.
Barry Thomas:
Barry Thomas won the Legs Open at Panmure in 2023 at one over par, settling a tie at the top with Colin Howieson on the countback — holes 1, 2, 17 and 18, where his two under beat Howieson's one over.

He had topped the Stableford that day as well, on 35 points, though the Main title took precedence and the Stableford passed to Howieson.

Three appearances in all: a no-return at St Andrews in 2020, the title in 2023, and 27th at Downfield in 2024.
David Burns:
David Burns won the Legs Open at Gullane in 2018 at two over par, leading the Stableford on 34 points in the same round.

It was the third of four appearances in five years. He had finished ninth at Lanark in 2015 and fourth at Dalmahoy in 2017, and returned in 2019 to finish tenth at Ladybank.
John Pow:
John Pow won the Legs Open at Dundonald Links in 2014 at two over par, and led the Stableford with 34 points.

He had finished fifth at Carnwath the year before, one under par, with a gross of 81 that was second only to the champion's. Those two championships are his only appearances, and at 70 he is the oldest man to have won the championship.
Steven Leisegang:
Steven Leisegang won the Legs Open at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, and did it from the worst possible start: seven at the opening hole and seven at the second left him five over par after two.

He recovered to a nett 75, three over, and finished two clear of Stevie Connelly. His 33 Stableford points were the best in the field, though the Main title carried the Stableford to Connelly instead.

He is the only South African to have played the championship.
Mark Alston:
Mark Alston has played every Legs Open. Fourteen championships from Carnwath in 2013 to Castle Stuart in 2026, a record he shares only with Robert Hamilton.

His best finishes bookend that run: tied third on debut in 2013, two under par, and tied third again at Blairgowrie in 2021 at level. In between came fourth at Southerness in 2016 and fifths at Dundonald Links and Gullane.

His handicap has come down from 24 to 13 over the fourteen years. Three of the last eight championships have ended without a card returned.
Robert Hamilton:
Robert Hamilton has played all fourteen Legs Opens, and is one of two men to have won the Stableford twice, with Stephen Magowan — at Lanark in 2015 with 33 points and at Balmedie in 2025 with 34.

The 2015 championship was his best afternoon: he took the Scratch title too, with an 83, and finished tied second in the Main. He went one better in 2025, second on his own at two over, a decade on.

There have been thirds at Southerness in 2016 and fourths at Dundonald Links in 2014 as well. His lowest round is the 82 he returned at Blairgowrie in 2021, where he was runner-up in the Scratch.
Stephen Magowan:
Stephen Magowan has twice won the Legs Open Stableford — at Gullane in 2018 with 32 points and at St Andrews in 2020 with 33 — and took the Scratch title in 2020 as well with an 86.

Both of those years he was also runner-up in the Main, four over par on each occasion. Only Robert Hamilton has also finished second twice without going on to win.

Eleven appearances since 2016 make him one of the championship's regulars, and at 60 one of its more senior ones.
Colum Watters:
Colum Watters has played eleven Legs Opens since 2016, though only five have produced a completed card.

When he has finished, he has gone close. Third at St Andrews in 2020, five over par, with a tied second in the Stableford on 33 points, and tied sixth at Ladybank the year before. His 93 at St Andrews remains his lowest round.

Six no-returns, including three of his first four appearances, is the most of any player on the roster.
David Pow:
David Pow has played nine Legs Opens across fourteen years, from Carnwath in 2013 to Castle Stuart in 2026.

His best finish is seventh at Loch Lomond in 2022, five over par. He was ninth at Dundonald Links in 2014 and eleventh on debut in 2013, where his 104 was good for eleventh in the Scratch.

Four of his last six championships have ended without a card. His handicap has moved the other way from most of the field, out from 20 to 24.
Toby Stanton:
Toby Stanton is the only Englishman to have played the Legs Open, with seven appearances between 2013 and 2023.

Sixth on debut at Carnwath in 2013, three over par, and tied sixth at Blairgowrie in 2021 at four over are his best returns. He was sixth in the Stableford in 2013 with 35 points.

Four of the seven have ended without a card returned.
Stevie Anderson:
Stevie Anderson has six appearances since 2021 and a third place at Panmure in 2023, four over par, where he was also third in the Stableford on 32 points and tied third in the Scratch with an 82.

Fifth at Blairgowrie in 2021 and sixth at Balmedie in 2025 round out a consistent record. His handicap has come down from 13 to 8 across the six years.
Andrew Spiers:
Andrew Spiers won the Legs Open Stableford at Blairgowrie in 2021 with 39 points, a total bettered only twice and equalled once.

He finished second in the Main that day as well, one under par, a shot behind Nick Ward. It is comfortably his best championship: eighth at Loch Lomond in 2022 is the only other finish inside the top ten, and three of his five appearances have ended without a card.
Bobby Ferguson:
Bobby Ferguson played the first two Legs Opens and won the Stableford in the first of them, with 40 points — a total matched only by Alastair Campbell, in the same championship, and never beaten since.

He tied for the Main title at Carnwath that year on four under par before losing the countback to Campbell, and his 81 was second in the Scratch. He returned in 2014 to finish third at Dundonald Links.
Davie Clelland:
Davie Clelland played twice, in 2014 and 2015, and took both the Stableford and the Scratch at Dundonald Links in 2014 — 32 points and a gross of 85.

He was runner-up in the Main that year at four over, and returned the following season to finish tied fifth at Lanark.
Bruce Cruickshanks:
Bruce Cruickshanks won the Legs Open Stableford at Dalmahoy in 2017 with 34 points, in a championship where he also tied for the Main title at two over before losing the countback to Colin Howieson.

His 87 was second in the Scratch that day. Three appearances in three years followed a consistent line: sixth at Gullane in 2018 and tied sixth at Ladybank in 2019.
Grahame Ingram:
Grahame Ingram played one Legs Open, at Southerness in 2016, and won the Stableford with 22 points.

It was the hardest championship on record — the title was won at seventeen over par — and his gross of 107 was third in the Scratch while his nett was second in the Main. At 71 he is the oldest man to have played.
Scott Ingram:
Scott Ingram won the Legs Open Stableford at Southerness in 2016, in the championship that produced the highest winning score in the event's history.

He was fifth in the Main that day and fourth in the Scratch. His five appearances are spread across thirteen years, from Carnwath in 2013 to a no-return at Castle Stuart in 2026, with a seventh at Dundonald Links in 2014 and a tied seventh at Lanark in 2015 in between.
John McAlpine:
John McAlpine won the Legs Open Stableford at Downfield in 2024 with 37 points — and did it without returning a card, having picked up at the 14th.

It is the only time a no-return has won a Legs Open competition. The Stableford treats a picked-up hole as a blank where the Main and the Scratch disqualify the round outright, and his 37 points were the best in the field regardless.

Four appearances, every one of them a no-return. His handicap has come down from 40 to 32.
Neal Eadie:
Neal Eadie won the Legs Open Stableford at Loch Lomond in 2022 with 34 points, taking it on the inward nine from a four-way tie — his 19 points coming home beat the other three outright.

He was tied second in the Main the same day, two over par, and his 77 was second in the Scratch. He returned to Panmure in 2023 for a tied sixth, and has played no others.
Doug Scott:
Doug Scott holds the lowest gross round in Legs Open history: the 74 he returned at Loch Lomond in 2022, which took the Scratch title and left him tied second in the Main.

He plays off the lowest handicaps in the field — scratch in 2022, plus one by 2023 — and has four appearances between 2022 and 2025, the last two ending without a card.
Tom Sinton:
Tom Sinton won the Legs Open Scratch at Panmure in 2023 with a 77, and was fourth in the Main that day.

He had been tied second at Loch Lomond the year before, two over par, with 34 points for a share of second in the Stableford. Four appearances in five years, and a handicap down from 7 to 5 at 62.
Andrew Oliphant:
Andrew Oliphant has won the Legs Open Scratch twice in three appearances — a 76 at Downfield in 2024 and an 82 at Castle Stuart in 2026 — and has never finished outside the top six in the Main.

Fourth on debut at two over, tied third at Balmedie in 2025 and sixth in 2026. Off two, he is among the lowest handicaps to have played, and his 76 is the fourth-lowest round the championship has seen.
George Burns:
George Burns won the Legs Open Scratch at Gullane in 2018 with an 86, and finished third in the Main that day at five over par.

He had been fifth at Dalmahoy the year before. Three appearances in three years, the last of them a no-return at Ladybank in 2019.
Stevie Connelly:
Stevie Connelly won the Legs Open Stableford at Castle Stuart in 2026 with 31 points, in the championship where he also finished runner-up in the Main, five over par and two behind Steven Leisegang.

It was a considerable step up. His three previous appearances had produced two no-returns and a tied seventeenth at Downfield in 2024.
Fraser Donaldson:
Fraser Donaldson was tied second at Downfield in 2024, one over par, and tied second in the Scratch the same day with a 77 — his lowest round.

Off a handicap of one, he is among the lowest in the field, which makes the 35 points that earned a share of third in the Stableford that year a considerable return. Five appearances since 2022, with a sixth at Loch Lomond on debut and a tied seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026.
John Taylor:
John Taylor's Legs Open career has two distinct halves. He played the first two championships, at Carnwath and Dundonald Links, finishing seventh and eighth, then did not appear again for a decade.

Since returning in 2024 he has been better than ever: tied fifth at Downfield, tied third at Balmedie in 2025 at six over with 32 points for a share of third in the Stableford, and tied ninth at Castle Stuart. His handicap has come down from 18 to 11 across the gap.
Owen Watters:
Owen Watters finished third at Ladybank in 2019, two over par, and was third in the Scratch the same day with an 86 — his best round and his best championship by some way.

His debut the year before had been one of the four cards lost at Gullane, when the closing group's scorecards were ruined by the weather and the digital scoring failed with them. Three of his five appearances ended without a return; the other produced a tied sixth at Panmure in 2023.
David McGowan:
David McGowan has played five consecutive championships since 2022 and finished every one of them — a record of reliability matched by few in the field.

His best is a tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025, nine over par. Tied eighth at Panmure in 2023, where his 88 was tied eighth in the Scratch, is the closest he has come to a low round.
Jim Yuille:
Jim Yuille finished third at Dalmahoy in 2017, five over par, with an 87 that was tied second in the Scratch and 31 points for a share of third in the Stableford — the best of his four appearances by a distance.

He had been sixth at Dundonald Links in 2014. The other two, in 2015 and 2020, ended without a card.
Iain MacLeod:
Iain MacLeod played four of the first five Legs Opens, finishing eighth at Carnwath in 2013 and tenth at Dundonald Links the following year.

His best Stableford came last, a share of third at Dalmahoy in 2017 with 31 points, alongside a tied eighth in the Main.
Martin McErlean:
Martin McErlean finished tied third at Blairgowrie in 2021, level par, on his debut — and took second place in the Stableford that day with 38 points, a total only four men have bettered.

He was playing off 42 at the time, second only to John McAlpine's 46 as the highest the championship has recorded. It has since come down to 29. His three appearances after that debut have all ended without a card.
Mark Kennedy:
Mark Kennedy has four appearances since 2023, three of which ended without a card returned.

The exception was Balmedie in 2025, where he finished tied fourteenth at twelve over par with a 92 for twelfth in the Scratch.
Colin Hart:
Colin Hart has improved in each of his three championships: tied fourteenth at Downfield in 2024, tied seventh at Balmedie in 2025, and tied fourth at Castle Stuart in 2026 at seven over par.

He took a share of third in the Stableford in 2025 with 32 points. His handicap has come down from 16 to 12 across the three years.
Ross Dick:
Ross Dick was tied fifth on his debut at Downfield in 2024, three over par, with a 84 for sixth in the Scratch and 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford.

At 26 he is the youngest man on the roster, and his handicap has come down sharply from 9 to 4 across three appearances. Tied tenth at Balmedie followed in 2025.
Brian McGuire:
Brian McGuire has finished all three of his championships, improving from tied ninth at Downfield in 2024 to tied seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026, ten over par.

His 86 at Downfield is his lowest round, and his handicap has come down from 9 to 6 in three years.
Ross McCallum:
Ross McCallum was tied ninth on his debut at Downfield in 2024, five over par, with 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford.

He returned a no-return at Balmedie the following year and was tied eighteenth at Castle Stuart in 2026.
Michael Holton:
Michael Holton finished tied tenth at Panmure in 2023 on his debut and tied fourteenth at Downfield the following year, where his 85 was seventh in the Scratch and his lowest round.

His third appearance, at Balmedie in 2025, ended without a card.
Gary Drummond:
Gary Drummond was tied ninth on his debut at Downfield in 2024, five over par, and his 79 that day was fourth in the Scratch, one of thirteen rounds under 80 in the championship's history.

He plays off plus one, among the lowest handicaps in the field. His two appearances since have both ended without a card.
Cameron Dyer: Cameron Dyer is, at 27, one of the three youngest men on the roster. His debut at Downfield in 2024 ended without a card, but he has finished both championships since: tied twelfth at Balmedie in 2025, eleven over par, and twenty-third at Castle Stuart in 2026.
Grant Robertson:
Grant Robertson has three appearances since 2023, two of which ended without a card.

The exception was Castle Stuart in 2026, where he finished tied eighteenth at sixteen over par with a 93 for fourteenth in the Scratch.
Ross Findlay:
Ross Findlay has played the last three championships and finished all three, his best a twenty-first at Balmedie in 2025.

At 27 he is among the youngest in the field, and his handicap has come down from 7 to 5 across the three years.
Stuart Hamilton:
Stuart Hamilton was tied second at Downfield in 2024, one over par, on his debut — taking a share of third in the Stableford with 35 points off a handicap of 20.

He returned to Balmedie the following year to finish twentieth, and has played no others.
Chris Peffers:
Chris Peffers finished tied ninth at Loch Lomond in 2022 on his debut, seven over par, with an 87 that was eighth in the Scratch.

He returned at Downfield in 2024 for a tied seventeenth.
Gerard Doyle:
Gerard Doyle was tied ninth on his debut at Downfield in 2024, five over par, with 33 points for a share of sixth in the Stableford and an 88 for a share of twelfth in the Scratch.

His second appearance, at Balmedie in 2025, ended without a card.
Keiran Dougan:
Keiran Dougan finished eighth at Downfield in 2024, four over par, off a handicap of 27 — the highest of anyone inside the top ten that year.

His debut at Panmure the season before had ended without a card, though his 29 Stableford points were still enough for a share of sixth.
Andy Lewis: Andy Lewis played twice, in 2016 and 2017. The first ended without a card; the second produced a tied eighth at Dalmahoy, ten over par, with an 88 that was fourth in the Scratch.
Roger McGuigan: Roger McGuigan finished tied twenty-first at Downfield in 2024 on his debut, nine over par. His second appearance, at Balmedie the following year, ended without a card.
Scott Findlay: Scott Findlay has played the last two championships, finishing nineteenth at Balmedie in 2025 and tied fifteenth at Castle Stuart in 2026, fourteen over par.
James Cannon:
James Cannon's debut at Balmedie in 2025 ended without a card, though his 29 Stableford points were still good for a share of seventh.

He finished tied twenty-fifth at Castle Stuart the following year, and has brought his handicap down from 13 to 9 across the two championships.
Stephen Brown:
Stephen Brown has played the last two championships and completed neither, picking up in both.

His 29 Stableford points at Balmedie in 2025 were still enough for a share of seventh, the Stableford counting a picked-up hole as a blank where the Main disqualifies the round.
Colin Speirs:
Colin Speirs finished third at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, six over par, with an 83 that was tied second in the Scratch and 30 points for a share of third in the Stableford.

Off a handicap of five, only the champion Steven Leisegang bettered him among the five men making their debut that year.
John Dundas:
John Dundas was tied fourth at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his debut, seven over par, with 30 points for a share of third in the Stableford and a 91 for a share of eighth in the Scratch.

His was one of the four cards caught by the delay in group two's scoring that day, which left the leaderboard without him for the first three hours of the championship.
Chris Merrilees:
Chris Merrilees finished twelfth at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, twelve over par, with a 92 for thirteenth in the Scratch.

He was in group two, whose scores did not reach the scoreboard until around the ninth.
Stephen McCall: Stephen McCall finished twenty-seventh at Castle Stuart in 2026 on his only appearance, with a 103.
Jamie Jordan: Jamie Jordan finished fourth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, nine over par, with a 93 that was fifth in the Scratch and 30 points for a share of fifth in the Stableford.
Gary Simpson: Gary Simpson finished tied fifth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, ten over par, and took a share of third in the Stableford with 31 points off a handicap of 20.
John Dick: John Dick finished tied seventh at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, eleven over par, off a handicap of 22 — the highest in that championship's top ten.
Jamie Bain: Jamie Bain finished tied tenth at Lanark in 2015 on his only appearance, sixteen over par, with a 102 for a share of eighth in the Scratch.
Steven Napier: Steven Napier finished tied sixth at St Andrews in 2020 on his only appearance, eleven over par, with a 99 that was eighth in the Scratch.
David Hogg: David Hogg finished twenty-sixth at Downfield in 2024 on his only appearance, fourteen over par, with a 98.
Alyn Peden: Alyn Peden played one Legs Open, at Lanark in 2015, and did not return a card — though his 27 Stableford points were still enough for a share of ninth.
Craig McMahon: Craig McMahon played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018, and did not return a card. His 22 Stableford points were seventh in a championship where four players finished on none at all.
Sandy Hogg: Sandy Hogg played one Legs Open, at Panmure in 2023, and did not return a card. Off a handicap of three, he was among the lowest in that field.
Stephen Reilly: Stephen Reilly played one Legs Open, at Balmedie in 2025, and did not return a card, though his 25 Stableford points were good for a share of nineteenth.
Danny Gardiner: Danny Gardiner played one Legs Open, at St Andrews in 2020, and withdrew injured after the opening hole. He finished on two Stableford points, both from that opening hole.
John Lyle:
John Lyle played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018, and finished on no points at all — one of four players in the closing group whose scorecards were destroyed by the weather, with the digital scoring failing alongside them.

None of the four returned a card, and none scored a point.
Paul Wright: Paul Wright played one Legs Open, at Gullane in 2018. He was in the closing group whose scorecards were ruined by the rain, the digital backup failing at the same time, and finished on no points — as did all four of them.
